title: Jev: the AI model that can't chat
notes: Facts checked 2026-10-11. typesafe.ai: Jev is 'our first System One Model' (early access); '193.6x Faster, 444.6x Cheaper' on TypeSafe's own System One workflow comparison (0.114 s and $0.000081 against 8.566 s and $0.013880 for LLMs); '$42' per billion input tokens; 'Made in SF'; 'an AI lab'. docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one: Jev evaluates a state (text, JSON) and typed questions and returns typed answers with probabilities, not text; it does not write replies, produce code or explain its reasoning; primitives Choice (one option of a set, e.g. billing / technical / account), Score (a value on a scale) and Noul (yes or no as a probability); confidence helps decide when to act and when to escalate to a person; the name comes from Kahneman's System 1 (fast, intuitive judgment); calibration 'does not guarantee that an individual answer is correct'. Output tokens are free; billed on input. The Register (2026-09-28): went viral; uses include classification and routing, guardrails for AI agents (which Unix commands an agent may run), and playing Doom; it cannot answer outside the options it is given; back-end proprietary. Weights not released; available through TypeSafe's API, OpenRouter, Cloudflare. Voice: ElevenLabs (Chris, eleven_v4).
